words.tip: Casual and works almost anywhere. Show how greetings change through the day (Guten Morgen, Guten Tag, Guten Abend) and regional ones like Moin or Servus.
Informal goodbye. Compare with the more formal Auf Wiedersehen, and with Bis später / Bis bald.
Teach the reply too: Bitte! or Gern geschehen. Danke schön and Vielen Dank are stronger.
A do-everything word: please, you're welcome, here you go, and 'Bitte?' for 'pardon?'. Act out each use.

examples.english: Excuse me, where is the station?

words.tip: On its own it both gets attention and apologises. Es tut mir leid is a more heartfelt 'I'm sorry'.
Not capitalised unless it starts a sentence, unlike English 'I'.
For friends, family, kids and each other. When to switch to the formal Sie is a great discussion topic.
Also means 'it' for masculine nouns: Der Kaffee? Er ist kalt. (The coffee? It's cold.)
One word, three meanings: sie = she, sie = they, and capitalised Sie = formal 'you'. The verb ending and context tell them apart.
Easy win: with wir the verb looks like the infinitive (wir gehen, wir kommen).
ist is the most common form of sein (to be). The whole set is irregular: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie sind. Worth chanting together a few times.
German uses haben where English uses 'to be': Ich habe Hunger (I'm hungry), Ich habe Recht (I'm right).
Covers both 'do' and 'make'. Handy phrase: Das macht nichts (never mind).

examples.english: Shall we go to the cinema today?

words.tip: Mainly going on foot. By car, train or bike Germans usually say fahren. Also: Wie geht's? = how's it going?
Practise asking and answering: Woher kommst du? Ich komme aus …

examples.english: What would you like to eat?

words.tip: Looks like English 'was' but means 'what'.
Classic trap for English speakers: wer = who, wo = where. Drill the pair together.
Location only. Woher = where from, wohin = where to.
Only for questions. In statements 'when' is wenn or als, which can wait until later.

examples.english: What's your name? (lit. how are you called?)

words.tip: Wie heißt du? is the normal way to ask someone's name.
Bonus word: doch is the 'yes' you use after a negative question (Kommst du nicht? Doch!). Nothing like it in English.
Nein, danke is the polite refusal. kein ('not a, no' before nouns) comes later.
Tends to drift towards the end of the sentence (Ich komme heute nicht), which feels odd at first.
Ich auch = me too. Ich auch nicht = me neither.
Also in Danke sehr and Bitte sehr.
Heute Abend = tonight. Heute Morgen = this morning.
Lowercase morgen = tomorrow, capitalised der Morgen = morning. So morgen früh = tomorrow morning.
Bis jetzt = until now, so far.

noun.hint: Times of day are der: der Tag, der Morgen, der Abend. The odd one out is die Nacht.

words.tip: Guten Tag is a polite hello. Jeden Tag = every day.

examples.text: Wir fahren jedes Jahr nach China.
examples.english: We go to China every year.

words.tip: Frohes neues Jahr! = Happy New Year. Talk about how each of you celebrates it.
Irregular present: du isst, er isst. Capitalised, das Essen = the food / the meal.

examples.english: Would you like something to drink?

words.tip: trinken, trank, getrunken follows the same pattern as English drink, drank, drunk.

noun.hint: Drinks are mostly der (der Kaffee, der Tee), but das Wasser and das Bier are exceptions.

examples.english: I drink a lot of water.

words.tip: In restaurants you'll be asked mit oder ohne Kohlensäure? (sparkling or still?). Tap water is Leitungswasser.
A point of German pride. Talk about favourites: Vollkornbrot, Brötchen (bread roll), Brezel.

noun.hint: Drinks are mostly der: der Kaffee, der Tee, der Wein. Exceptions: das Wasser, das Bier.

words.tip: Kaffee und Kuchen (coffee and cake in the afternoon) is a tradition worth explaining.
Two key phrases: nach Hause (going home) and zu Hause (at home).
Same in singular and plural. Builds Wohnzimmer (living room), Schlafzimmer (bedroom), Badezimmer (bathroom).
Tür auf / Tür zu = door open / door shut.
wohnen = to reside somewhere. leben = to be alive, to live a life. die Wohnung = flat/apartment.
ins Bett gehen = go to bed. Pair it with Gute Nacht!

noun.hint: People usually take their sex: die Mutter, der Vater, die Frau, der Mann.

words.tip: Mama in everyday speech. The plural adds an umlaut: Mütter.

noun.hint: People usually take their sex: der Vater, die Mutter, der Mann, die Frau.

words.tip: Papa in everyday speech. Umlaut in the plural again: Väter.

noun.hint: Das Kind stays neuter whoever the child is, like das Baby.

examples.english: The child is playing in the garden.

words.tip: Neuter (das Kind) whatever the child's gender. Plural Kinder, as in kindergarten.

noun.hint: Male people are der. A female friend is die Freundin, and -in endings are always die.

words.tip: mein Freund often means 'my boyfriend'. To be clear, say ein Freund (von mir). Feminine die Freundin works the same way.
Stress the second syllable: fa-MI-li-e, four syllables.
False friend: ich will = I want, not I will. The future uses werden.

examples.english: My parents like you a lot.

words.tip: ich mag = I like. ich möchte = I would like, the polite form for ordering.
Put gern after a verb to say you like doing it: Ich koche gern. Gern geschehen = you're welcome.
Glück means both luck and happiness, so glücklich can be either. Viel Glück! = good luck.
todmüde = dead tired. Compare with Chinese 累死了 (tired to death) from the same session.
Also the adverb 'well': Du sprichst gut Deutsch. Irregular comparison: gut, besser, am besten.
Big for things, tall for people. ß sounds like 'ss', and in capitals it's often written GROSS.
The ending changes before a noun (ein kleines Haus, eine kleine Wohnung). Don't drill the endings yet, just point them out.
You've met it already in Frohes neues Jahr. It shows up in place names too: Neustadt = new town.

examples.text: Mein Handy ist schon sehr alt.
examples.english: My phone is already very old.

words.tip: Works for people and things alike, unlike Chinese 老 / 旧. Practise: Ich bin … Jahre alt.
Eins when counting; before a noun it becomes ein / eine (ein Kaffee, eine Tür). Show German finger counting: it starts with the thumb.
On the phone people often say zwo so it can't be confused with drei.

examples.text: Das Kind ist drei Jahre alt.
examples.english: The child is three years old.

words.tip: A good word for practising the German r, made at the back of the throat.
Sounds like English 'fear'. Viertel (quarter) comes from it: Viertel nach vier = quarter past four.
A test of the ü sound: say 'ee' with your lips rounded.
Also the answer at roll call. Hier, bitte = here you go.
Clearly 'over there'. Da is the casual all-rounder.

examples.english: I'll be there in a moment.

words.tip: Very flexible: there, here (Ich bin gleich da = I'll be right there), and 'then'. Point and say da!

examples.english: The door is on the left.
We have to go left here.

words.tip: Nach links = to the left. Practise giving each other directions around the house.

examples.english: The kitchen is on the right.

words.tip: Fun fact for driving: rechts vor links (right before left) is the right-of-way rule at unmarked crossings.

examples.text: Wir trinken Kaffee und essen Kuchen.
examples.english: We drink coffee and eat cake.

examples.text: Ich bin müde und habe Hunger.

words.tip: On its own, Und? means 'So? How did it go?'

examples.english: Are you coming today or tomorrow?

words.tip: At the end of a sentence it means 'right?': Du kommst mit, oder?

examples.text: Ich will kommen, aber ich muss arbeiten.
examples.english: I want to come, but I have to work.

words.tip: Also adds feeling: Das ist aber schön! = Oh, that's lovely!

examples.text: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich müde bin.
examples.english: I'm staying home because I'm tired.

examples.text: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich dich liebe.
examples.english: I'm learning German because I love you.

words.tip: Sends the verb to the very end (weil ich müde bin). A first taste of German word order.
mitkommen = to come along, from session 2's Kommst du mit? Also 'by': mit dem Auto = by car.

examples.text: Wie kann man das auf Deutsch sagen?
examples.english: How do you say that in German?

examples.text: Kannst du das noch einmal sagen?

words.tip: Wie sagt man … auf Deutsch? is the most useful sentence for these sessions.
Irregular: du siehst, er sieht. fernsehen = to watch TV, literally 'far-see'.
Hearing and listening: Musik hören. gehören = to belong to.

examples.english: I'd really like to know that.

words.tip: Knowing facts. For people and places use kennen. Irregular: ich weiß, du weißt, er weiß.

examples.english: We've known each other for a long time.

examples.text: Meine Eltern kennen dich noch nicht.
examples.english: My parents don't know you yet.

words.tip: Being familiar with someone or something. Chinese makes exactly the same split (知道 vs 认识), so compare them together.

examples.text: Wir können auch zu Hause bleiben.

words.tip: A modal verb: the second verb goes to the end. Also 'know how to': Ich kann Deutsch.

examples.english: Do we have to work tomorrow?

words.tip: Trap: ich muss nicht = I don't have to, not 'I mustn't'.

examples.english: We're not allowed to park here.

words.tip: Permission. Du darfst nicht = you mustn't, which is the real 'mustn't'.

examples.english: The children are supposed to sleep now.

words.tip: Often about what someone else wants: Ich soll Brot kaufen = I'm supposed to buy bread.

examples.text: Die Kinder werden so schnell groß.
examples.english: The kids are growing up so fast.

words.tip: Also makes the future: Ich werde kommen = I will come. Remember ich will = I want (session 10).

examples.text: Ich gehe heute in die Stadt.
alternatives: Heute gehe ich in die Stadt.

words.tip: in die Stadt gehen = to go into town. Umlaut in the plural: Städte.
Germans live in a street, not on it. Swiss German writes Strasse.

noun.hint: Short words from other languages ending in -o are usually das: das Auto, das Kino, das Büro.

words.tip: Plural with -s, unusual in German. mit dem Auto = by car.
Any trip by car, train or bike, whereas gehen is on foot. Past tense with sein: ich bin gefahren.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: der Hof, so der Bahnhof.

examples.text: Ich hole dich am Bahnhof ab.
examples.english: I'll pick you up at the station.

words.tip: Bahn (rail) + Hof (yard). Hauptbahnhof (Hbf) = main station. Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof = it's all Greek to me.

examples.english: I have a lot of work today.

words.tip: zur Arbeit gehen = to go to work. Arbeitsplatz = workplace.

examples.text: Wir arbeiten beide in der Stadt.

words.tip: The extra e (du arbeitest, er arbeitet) keeps the t audible. Talk about what each of you does all day.

examples.text: Wir lernen jeden Tag fünf Wörter.
examples.english: We learn five words every day.

words.tip: Learning anything, including revising for exams. studieren is only for university.

examples.text: Die Kinder sind in der Schule.

words.tip: For children. University is die Uni. Grundschule = primary school.

examples.english: I'm reading a book at the moment.

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Bücher. Bücherei = library, Buchhandlung = bookshop.

examples.text: Ich arbeite diese Woche zu Hause.
examples.english: I'm working from home this week.
alternatives: Diese Woche arbeite ich zu Hause.

words.tip: Wochenende = weekend. diese Woche / nächste Woche = this week / next week.

noun.hint: Times of day are der: der Abend, der Morgen, der Tag. The odd one out is die Nacht.

examples.text: Am Abend sehen wir einen Film.
examples.english: In the evening we're watching a film.
alternatives: Wir sehen am Abend einen Film.

words.tip: heute Abend = tonight. Abendessen = dinner.

noun.hint: The odd one out: der Morgen, der Tag, der Abend, but die Nacht.

examples.text: In der Nacht ist es kalt.
alternatives: Es ist in der Nacht kalt.

words.tip: Gute Nacht is only for bedtime. As a greeting in the evening, use Guten Abend.
Wie spät ist es? = what time is it? Careful: halb vier means half past three (literally 'half to four').

examples.english: We still have plenty of time.

words.tip: Time as an amount (Zeit haben). For clock time use Uhr. Keine Zeit! = no time!

examples.english: We still need to buy bread.

examples.text: Ich will ein neues Auto kaufen.
examples.english: I want to buy a new car.

words.tip: verkaufen = to sell, einkaufen = to go shopping. Prefixes change the meaning a lot in German.

examples.english: That costs a lot of money.

words.tip: Usually no plural (Gelder means funds). Bargeld = cash. A good chance to practise kein.
Was kostet das? is the shopping question. kosten also means 'to taste' food.
viel (much) vs viele (many): viel Geld, viele Leute. Vielen Dank = many thanks.

examples.text: Die Wohnung ist schön, aber teuer.
examples.english: The flat is nice but expensive.

words.tip: The opposite is billig (cheap) or günstig (good value). Drops an e before endings: ein teures Auto.

examples.text: Ich stehe um sechs Uhr auf.

words.tip: The chs sounds like 'x': zex.
The -en drops in bigger numbers: siebzehn (17), siebzig (70).
The ch is the throaty sound in 'Bach'. achten = to pay attention.
eu sounds like English 'oy': noyn.
z sounds like 'ts'. The teens add -zehn: dreizehn, vierzehn. Bigger numbers say the ones first: neunundneunzig = 'nine-and-ninety'.

noun.hint: People usually take their sex: der Mann, die Frau.

examples.text: Der Mann dort ist mein Vater.
examples.english: The man over there is my father.

words.tip: mein Mann = my husband. Don't confuse with lowercase man (one, you): Man sagt… = people say…

noun.hint: People usually take their sex: die Frau, der Mann.

words.tip: Three in one: woman, wife (meine Frau) and the title Mrs/Ms (Frau Schmidt).

noun.hint: Der Mensch means any person, whatever their sex.

words.tip: Gets an -en in most cases: den Menschen. On its own, Mensch! is an exclamation like 'Man!'

examples.english: The girl is reading a book.

words.tip: Neuter, because the -chen ending ('little') always makes a noun neuter. Grammar beats biology.
Wie ist dein Name? is a bit more formal than Wie heißt du?
Takes the same endings as ein: mein Buch, meine Tür, meinen Kaffee.
Goes with du. The formal 'your' is capitalised Ihr.
unsere Wohnung = our flat. The -er is part of the word, not an ending.
Her and their, and capitalised Ihr is formal 'your'. Context decides, just like sie.
Alle zusammen! = all together! Compare Chinese 大家 from the same session.
Schlaf gut! = sleep well. Schlafzimmer (bedroom) from session 8 uses it.

examples.english: What do you want to read?

words.tip: Irregular: du liest, er liest. vorlesen = to read aloud.

examples.text: Kannst du mir eine Nachricht schreiben?
examples.english: Can you send me a message?

words.tip: Wie schreibt man das? = how do you spell that? You'll ask it a lot.

examples.english: The kids are playing in the park.

words.tip: Games, sports and instruments all use spielen: Fußball spielen, Klavier spielen. Chinese splits these up.
warten auf = wait for. Warte mal! = hang on!

examples.text: Kannst du mir bitte das Buch geben?
examples.english: Can you give me the book, please?

words.tip: es gibt = there is / there are: Es gibt Kaffee. One of the most useful phrases in German.
Ich nehme… is how you order. Irregular: du nimmst, er nimmt.
mitbringen = to bring along. The past gebracht is irregular, like denken → gedacht.
Takes dir, not dich: ich helfe dir. Hilfe! = help!
gebraucht also means second-hand. Du brauchst nicht zu kommen = you don't need to come.
denken an = to think of someone. Ich denke, dass… = I think that…
Both 'believe' and the everyday 'I reckon'. Das glaube ich nicht! = I don't believe it!
For languages and conversations. Irregular: du sprichst, er spricht. Compare sagen (to say) from session 15.
die Frage = the question. fragen is asking a question; asking for something is bitten.
Verstanden? = got it? Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof from session 17 is its funnier cousin.
A favourite German small-talk topic. Schönes Wetter heute! = lovely weather today!
Feminine (die Sonne) but der Mond (the moon) is masculine. Sonntag = Sunday, the sun's day.

noun.hint: Weather words are mostly der: der Regen, der Schnee, der Wind.

words.tip: Es regnet = it's raining. Regenschirm = umbrella ('rain shield').
I'm warm is Mir ist warm (literally 'to me it's warm'). Ich bin warm means something else entirely.

examples.text: Im Winter ist es sehr kalt.

words.tip: Same pattern: Mir ist kalt = I'm cold. Compare Chinese 我很冷, which says it directly.
Rotwein = red wine. rot werden = to blush.
blau sein also means to be drunk! blaumachen = to skip work.
Another ü to practise. Die Grünen = the Green party.
schwarzfahren = riding without a ticket. Take the sch-w-arz-tz slowly.
Spelled exactly like ich weiß (I know) from session 15. Context tells them apart.
immer noch = still. für immer = forever.
Wie oft? = how often? Comparative: öfter.
noch nie = never yet: Ich war noch nie in China = I've never been to China.
Also a softener with no direct translation: Das ist schon gut = that's fine, really.
noch nicht = not yet. noch einmal = once more, handy when practising.
… tut weh = … hurts. Kopfschmerzen = headache.
A mobile phone is a Handy in German, and 手机 ('hand machine') in Chinese.
Augenblick = moment ('blink of an eye'). unter vier Augen = in private.
Krankenhaus = hospital ('sick house'). Gute Besserung! = get well soon.

noun.hint: Male people are der. A female doctor is die Ärztin, and -in endings are always die.

examples.english: I have to go to the doctor.

words.tip: A female doctor is die Ärztin. zum Arzt gehen = to go to the doctor.
Singular in German where English says 'clothes': Die Kleidung ist neu. Casually people say Klamotten.
One Hose is one pair of trousers, so it's singular: eine Hose, not 'a pair of'. Unterhose = underpants.
Hausschuhe = slippers, Handschuh = glove ('hand shoe'). Talk about whether shoes come off at the door in your homes.

examples.english: What do you want to wear today?

words.tip: Both 'wear' and 'carry': Ich trage den Koffer. Umlaut in du trägst, er trägt.

examples.english: I still have to get dressed.

words.tip: Separable: the an jumps to the end (Ich ziehe die Schuhe an). sich anziehen = to get dressed, ausziehen = to take off.

examples.text: Wir essen heute in der Küche.
examples.english: We're eating in the kitchen today.

words.tip: Also 'cuisine': die deutsche Küche. Practise Küche vs Kuchen (cake): only the ü and the ending tell them apart.
Also 'to boil': Das Wasser kocht. der Koch / die Köchin = the cook.

examples.text: Das Essen steht auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: The food is on the table.

words.tip: den Tisch decken = to set the table. Schreibtisch = desk ('writing table').
Same in singular and plural. Not a bank teller! Suppenteller = soup bowl.
No 'of': ein Glas Wasser. Glasses for your eyes are die Brille. Show the Prost! ritual: clink and keep eye contact.

examples.text: Ich esse jeden Tag einen Apfel.
examples.english: I eat an apple every day.

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Äpfel. Apfelschorle (apple juice with sparkling water) is a very German drink.
A collective word with no plural. One piece is ein Stück Obst. die Frucht exists but is more technical.

noun.hint: Despite the -e, it's das. Many nouns starting with Ge- are das: das Gemüse, das Geschenk, das Getränk.

words.tip: Singular in German where English says 'vegetables': Das Gemüse ist frisch. Obst und Gemüse = fruit and veg.
Types build on it: Rindfleisch (beef), Schweinefleisch (pork). Ich bin Vegetarier / Vegetarierin is worth knowing.

examples.text: Ich esse jeden Morgen ein Ei.
examples.english: I eat an egg every morning.

words.tip: Plural Eier. Spiegelei = fried egg ('mirror egg'), Rührei = scrambled egg.

examples.english: Shall we go to a restaurant today?

words.tip: Pronounced the French way, with a nasal ending and no t. ins Restaurant gehen = to eat out.
be- verbs take no ge-: ich habe bestellt. Also for ordering online. Practise Ich nehme… and Ich hätte gern…
Zahlen, bitte! works too. Expect Zusammen oder getrennt? (together or separately?) and explain rounding up with Stimmt so.
The everyday compliment for food: Mmh, lecker! Before a noun it takes endings: ein leckerer Kuchen.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: die Karte, so die Speisekarte.

words.tip: Speise (dish) + Karte (card). False friend: das Menü is a set meal. Getränkekarte = drinks menu.

examples.text: Die Reise war lang, aber schön.
examples.english: The trip was long but lovely.

words.tip: Gute Reise! = have a good trip. reisen = to travel, Reisepass = passport.

examples.text: Wir fliegen im Sommer nach China.
examples.english: We're flying to China in the summer.

words.tip: Past with sein: Ich bin nach Berlin geflogen. der Flug = the flight.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Zeug, so das Flugzeug.

examples.text: Das Flugzeug landet um acht Uhr.
examples.english: The plane lands at eight o'clock.

words.tip: Flug (flight) + Zeug (stuff, things): literally a 'flying thing'. Flughafen = airport ('flight harbour').
Same in singular and plural. den Koffer packen = to pack. Not to be confused with der Kaffee!

examples.english: We're going on holiday in Italy.

words.tip: Urlaub machen = to go on holiday, im Urlaub sein = to be on holiday. Ferien is for school and university holidays.
Irregular comparison: nah, näher, am nächsten. nächste Woche (next week) is the same word. in der Nähe = nearby.

examples.text: Ist es weit bis zum Bahnhof?
examples.english: Is it far to the station?

words.tip: Wie weit ist es? = how far is it? weit weg = far away. Also 'wide, loose' for clothes: Die Hose ist zu weit.
Says where something is. For movement use nach oben (going up). oben links = top left.
The partner of oben. Movement is nach unten. Point around the house and practise oben / unten / links / rechts.
Location takes the dative (neben dem Tisch), movement the accusative (neben mich). Just point out the pattern for now.

examples.text: Am Wochenende besuchen wir meine Mutter.
examples.english: We're visiting my mother at the weekend.

words.tip: No ge- in the past: ich habe besucht. der Besuch = visit or visitors: Wir haben Besuch = we have guests.

examples.text: Wir treffen uns um acht am Bahnhof.
examples.english: We're meeting at eight at the station.

words.tip: sich treffen = to meet up by arrangement. Meeting someone for the first time is kennenlernen. Irregular: du triffst, er trifft.

examples.english: When is the train supposed to arrive?

words.tip: Separable, with sein in the past. Bist du gut angekommen? (did you get there OK?) is the classic caring text.
Uses sein in the past even though nobody moves: Ich bin zu Hause geblieben. Bleib gesund! = stay healthy.
Often a separable prefix: zurückkommen, zurückrufen (call back). hin und zurück = there and back, a return ticket.

noun.hint: Days, months and seasons are all der. And Montag ends in der Tag.

examples.english: I have to work on Monday.

words.tip: am Montag = on Monday, montags = on Mondays. Go through the week; in the north Samstag is also called Sonnabend.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Ende, so das Wochenende.

examples.english: At the weekend we sleep in.

words.tip: am Wochenende = at the weekend. Schönes Wochenende! is what everyone says on a Friday.
gestern Abend = last night. vorgestern = the day before yesterday, übermorgen = the day after tomorrow.
morgen früh = tomorrow morning. Frühstück = breakfast ('early piece'), and Frühling (spring) is coming next session.
Wie spät ist es? = what time is it? zu spät = (too) late: Ich bin zu spät. Bis später! = see you later.

noun.hint: Time words are mostly der: der Tag, der Monat, der Abend, and every month and season. The odd ones out: die Woche, das Jahr, die Nacht.

examples.text: Nächsten Monat fliegen wir nach China.
examples.english: We're flying to China next month.

words.tip: Go through the months together. im Mai = in May, and im works for every month and season.

noun.hint: Days, months and seasons are all der.

examples.text: Im Sommer ist es lange hell.
examples.english: In summer it stays light for a long time.

words.tip: im Sommer = in summer. Sommerzeit = daylight saving time.

noun.hint: Days, months and seasons are all der.

examples.text: Im Winter trinken wir viel Tee.
examples.english: In winter we drink a lot of tea.

words.tip: Spelled like English but the W sounds like 'v'. A good moment to talk about Weihnachtsmärkte (Christmas markets).

noun.hint: Days, months and seasons are all der.

examples.text: Im Frühling wird es wieder warm.
examples.english: In spring it gets warm again.

words.tip: früh + -ling: the 'early' season. Watch out: the common synonym is das Frühjahr, which is neuter.

noun.hint: Days, months and seasons are all der.

examples.text: Im Herbst werden die Blätter rot.
examples.english: In autumn the leaves turn red.

words.tip: Related to English 'harvest'. The rbst cluster is a mouthful, so say it slowly together.
Sei nicht traurig = don't be sad. The final -ig sounds like 'ich' in standard German, 'ick' in the south.
Angst haben vor = to be afraid of, another haben where English uses 'be' (like Hunger haben). Keine Angst! = don't worry.
Strong and serious. Ich hab dich lieb is a warmer, lighter 'love you', also for family and friends. For things, use mögen or gern.
lachen über = to laugh about. lächeln = to smile. The ch is the throaty 'Bach' sound.
Sounds like der Wein (wine) but has nothing to do with it. Wein nicht! = don't cry.

noun.hint: Loanwords often borrow the gender of a German word: das Telefon, so das Handy.

words.tip: Looks English but isn't used that way in English. leer = flat battery; das Handy laden = to charge it.

examples.text: Ich kann dich heute Abend anrufen.

words.tip: Separable, and it takes dich, not dir: Ruf mich an! der Anruf = the call.
die Nachrichten = the news on TV. Chinese 消息 from the same session also means both message and news.

noun.hint: Short words from other languages ending in -o are usually das: das Foto, das Auto, das Kino.

examples.text: Mach mal ein Foto von uns!

words.tip: You make a photo in German: ein Foto machen, not nehmen. Plural with -s like Auto.

noun.hint: Machines ending in -er are usually der: der Computer, der Drucker, der Fernseher.

words.tip: Same in singular and plural. People also say der Rechner or der Laptop.
Also 'just': Mach es einfach! = just do it! On tickets, einfach = one-way.
schwer is the everyday alternative and also means heavy. Compare: Der Koffer ist schwer.
Nicht so schnell, bitte! is a must for these sessions. On its own, Schnell! = hurry up!
Also 'gradually, by now': Ich habe langsam Hunger = I'm starting to get hungry.
The opposite is richtig. On the phone: Falsch verbunden! = wrong number.
Separable and irregular: du fängst an, er fängt an. beginnen means the same but isn't separable.
Separable: Es hört auf zu regnen. Hör auf! = stop it! aufhören mit = to quit (a habit).
The verb stays in second place, so it jumps before the subject: Zuerst trinken wir, not Zuerst wir trinken.
Same word order as zuerst: Dann gehen wir. Bis dann! = see you then. Don't mix it up with denn.
Last in a list of steps. 'Finally, at long last' is endlich. Also: Wann hast du sie zuletzt gesehen? = when did you last see her?
Same in singular and plural. Explain Lüften: Germans throw the windows wide open for a few minutes, even in winter.
Umlaut in the plural: Stühle. Rollstuhl = wheelchair.
Same in singular and plural. Good practice for sch + ü together.
Licht an / Licht aus, or separable anmachen / ausmachen. The ch is the soft sound in ich.
Plural with -s. Careful: the synonym die Couch is feminine.

examples.english: The dog wants to go out.

words.tip: The final d sounds like t: hunt. Gassi gehen = to walk the dog.

examples.text: Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa.
examples.english: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

words.tip: A tomcat is der Kater, which also means a hangover!

examples.text: Im Garten steht ein großer Baum.
examples.english: There's a big tree in the garden.

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Bäume. Weihnachtsbaum = Christmas tree.

examples.text: Welches Tier magst du am liebsten?
examples.english: Which animal do you like best?

words.tip: Haustier = pet, Tierarzt = vet (Arzt from session 30). Related to English 'deer'.
in die Berge fahren = to go to the mountains. über den Berg sein = to be over the worst.

examples.english: What music do you like listening to?

words.tip: Stress the end: mu-SIK. Musik hören = listen to music, Musik machen = play music.

examples.text: Ich mache dreimal pro Woche Sport.
examples.english: I exercise three times a week.

words.tip: Sport machen = to work out, any kind of exercise. Different sports are Sportarten.
singen, sang, gesungen, just like sing, sang, sung. Teach each other a song!
z sounds like 'ts'. du tanzt: the extra s disappears into the z.

examples.text: Sollen wir heute Abend einen Film sehen?
examples.english: Shall we watch a film tonight?

words.tip: einen Film sehen, or casually gucken / schauen. ins Kino gehen = to go to the cinema.
eine Frage stellen = to ask a question. Keine Frage! = no doubt about it.
Watch out: it contains das Wort, but it's die Antwort, an exception to the compound rule. Point that out.

examples.english: You don't have to answer straight away.

words.tip: Answer a person with the dative (Antworte mir!), a question with auf (auf eine Frage antworten). Extra e like arbeiten.
Also softens requests: Kannst du mir vielleicht helfen? Pronounced fee-LEICHT.
Of course as an adverb, natural as an adjective. Klar! is the casual 'sure!'.
No ge- in the past: ich habe bezahlt. Cash is still common in Germany, so this question is worth knowing.
Can sound like 'cheap and nasty'. günstig (good value) is the more positive word.

examples.text: Der Laden macht um acht zu.

words.tip: Lowercase laden = to load or charge (das Handy laden). Explain that most shops are closed on Sundays.
Plural Firmen. Any company, big or small. bei einer Firma arbeiten = to work for a company.

examples.text: Was ist das für ein Ding?
examples.english: What kind of thing is that?

words.tip: die Sache is the other common word for 'thing'. Casually the plural is Dinger (thingies).

examples.english: We're getting married in the summer.

words.tip: No 'get' needed: Wir heiraten. verheiratet = married (status). Willst du mich heiraten?

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: die Zeit, so die Hochzeit.

words.tip: hoch (high) + Zeit (time), but the o is short here, unlike in hoch. Talk about wedding traditions like the Polterabend.

examples.text: Wir sind seit drei Jahren zusammen.
examples.english: We've been together for three years.

words.tip: zusammen sein = to be a couple. Note seit + present tense for 'have been … for'.
Irregular endings: dem Herzen, des Herzens. Herzlichen Glückwunsch! = congratulations, from the heart.
No ge- in the past: ich habe dich vermisst. Du fehlst mir is a softer way to say it.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: der Tag, so der Geburtstag.

words.tip: Never wish someone happy birthday early in Germany, it's bad luck. The birthday person often brings the cake.

noun.hint: Many nouns starting with Ge- are das: das Geschenk, das Gemüse, das Getränk.

examples.text: Das ist ein Geschenk für dich.
examples.english: This is a present for you.

words.tip: False friend: das Gift means poison! schenken = to give as a present.
Also just 'to party': feiern gehen = to go out partying. Feierabend = the end of the working day.

noun.hint: Loanwords often borrow the gender of a German word: die Feier, so die Party.

examples.english: Are you coming to my party?

words.tip: The plural is spelled Partys in German, not Parties. A party you throw at home is also eine Feier.

examples.english: Happy birthday from both of us!

words.tip: Takes dir, not dich. -ieren verbs have no ge-: ich habe gratuliert. Herzlichen Glückwunsch! is the set phrase.

words.gloss: to get up, to stand up

examples.english: We have to get up early tomorrow.

words.tip: Separable: Ich stehe um sieben auf. Past with sein: Ich bin spät aufgestanden. Also 'to stand up' from a chair.

examples.english: I just want to have a quick shower.

words.tip: Often reflexive: sich duschen. die Dusche = the shower. No 'take' needed: Ich dusche.

examples.text: Wir müssen noch die Zähne putzen.
examples.english: We still have to brush our teeth.

words.tip: Zähne putzen = brush your teeth, literally 'clean teeth'. Also for cleaning the house: das Bad putzen.

examples.text: Der Spiegel im Bad ist kaputt.
examples.english: The mirror in the bathroom is broken.

words.tip: Same in singular and plural. Der Spiegel is also a well-known news magazine, and Spiegelei (fried egg) comes from it.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Tuch, so das Handtuch.

examples.text: Kannst du mir ein Handtuch geben?
examples.english: Can you give me a towel?

words.tip: Hand + Tuch (cloth), used for any towel, even a big one. Point out the umlaut plural: Handtücher.

examples.text: Gib mir bitte mal das Salz.

words.tip: salzig = salty. Salz und Pfeffer = salt and pepper. The z sounds like 'ts'.

examples.text: Nimmst du Zucker in den Kaffee?
examples.english: Do you take sugar in your coffee?

words.tip: Zucker haben is casual for having diabetes. The z sounds like 'ts', so it's 'tsucker'.
Irregular past: geschnitten. Sich die Haare schneiden lassen = to get a haircut. das Messer = the knife.

examples.text: Wir müssen das Gemüse noch waschen.
examples.english: We still have to wash the vegetables.

words.tip: Umlaut in du wäschst, er wäscht. sich die Hände waschen = to wash your hands. Waschmaschine = washing machine.
Also 'cute', for babies, animals and partners: Du bist süß! The ß sounds like a sharp s.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Stück, so das Frühstück.

words.tip: früh (early) + Stück (piece). frühstücken = to have breakfast. Show off a German breakfast with Brötchen.
The ch after l is the soft sound in ich. Hafermilch = oat milk.

examples.text: Der Käse ist aus der Schweiz.

words.tip: So ein Käse! = what nonsense! Same in singular and plural.

examples.text: Isst du Butter auf dem Brot?
examples.english: Do you put butter on your bread?

words.tip: Feminine in standard German, though some southern speakers say der Butter. Alles in Butter! = everything's fine.

examples.english: I like drinking juice in the morning.

words.tip: Orangensaft (O-Saft for short) and Apfelsaft. Also juice for your phone, casually: Ich habe keinen Saft mehr.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: der Markt, so der Supermarkt.

examples.text: Der Supermarkt ist gleich um die Ecke.
examples.english: The supermarket is just around the corner.

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Supermärkte. Mention bringing your own bag and the Pfand (deposit) on bottles.

examples.text: Wollen wir im Park spazieren gehen?
examples.english: Shall we go for a walk in the park?

words.tip: Plural Parks. parken (to park a car) is a different word: der Parkplatz = parking space.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Haus, so das Krankenhaus.

words.tip: krank (ill) + Haus: a 'house for the sick'. im Krankenhaus = in hospital. Klinik is a common synonym.

examples.text: Die Bank ist am Samstag zu.
examples.english: The bank is closed on Saturday.

words.tip: Also 'bench', but then the plural is Bänke, not Banken. Sit on one in the park to make the point.

examples.text: Ich bringe das Paket zur Post.
examples.english: I'm taking the parcel to the post office.

words.tip: Both the post office and the mail itself: Hast du Post für mich? Explain the yellow Deutsche Post.

examples.text: Der Bus kommt in fünf Minuten.
examples.english: The bus is coming in five minutes.

words.tip: Plural with double s: Busse. mit dem Bus fahren = to go by bus; you 'drive' with every vehicle in German.

examples.text: Der Zug hat zehn Minuten Verspätung.
examples.english: The train is ten minutes late.

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Züge. A good moment to grumble together about Deutsche Bahn delays.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Rad, so das Fahrrad.

examples.text: Ich fahre mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit.

words.tip: Often shortened to das Rad: Rad fahren = to cycle. Umlaut in the plural: Fahrräder.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: die Bahn, so die U-Bahn.

words.tip: U is short for Untergrund. The S-Bahn is the suburban train. Pronounce the U like 'oo'.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: die Karte, so die Fahrkarte.

examples.english: Have you got a ticket yet?

words.tip: For trains and buses; a concert ticket is eine Karte or ein Ticket. Explain stamping it (entwerten) where needed.
Not 'bone' (that's der Knochen). Jemandem ein Bein stellen = to trip someone up.
Lowercase arm means poor: Er ist arm. in den Arm nehmen = to hug.
The final d sounds like t. Umlaut in the plural: Münder. Halt den Mund! = shut up (rude).
Die Nase voll haben = to be fed up ('have your nose full'). Point at faces and practise the body words.
Plural Ohren. Ohrwurm ('ear worm') = a song stuck in your head.
Usually plural: Kopfschmerzen (headache), Bauchschmerzen (stomach ache). Ich habe Schmerzen = I'm in pain.

examples.english: I think I've got a temperature.

words.tip: Fieber haben = to have a temperature. Fieber messen = take someone's temperature, in Celsius.

noun.hint: Loanwords ending in -ment are mostly das: das Medikament, das Dokument, das Instrument.

words.tip: die Medizin is more the science; for pills people also say Tabletten. Stress the end: me-di-ka-MENT.
For people and food. Bleib gesund! = stay healthy. The opposite is krank, which they already know.

examples.text: Die Apotheke ist am Sonntag zu.
examples.english: The pharmacy is closed on Sunday.

words.tip: Look for the red A sign. Medicine is only sold here, not in supermarkets; a Drogerie sells toiletries.
Used for people. Das ist nett von dir = that's kind of you. In some contexts 'nett' can sound a bit lukewarm.
Both funny and fun: Die Party war lustig. Careful: komisch usually means strange, not funny-haha.
Comparison with umlaut: klüger, am klügsten. schlau and intelligent are close synonyms.
Also for places: eine ruhige Straße. As a particle it softens: Komm ruhig rein = feel free to come in.
Used everywhere: Schönes Wochenende!, Schön, dich zu sehen! Practise the ö by rounding your lips for 'e'.

examples.english: I don't have much time today.

words.tip: Plural: wenige (few). ein wenig = a little, a bit, like ein bisschen. zu wenig = too little.
Can go before or after the noun: genug Geld or Geld genug. Jetzt reicht's! is another way to say 'enough!'.

examples.text: Ich möchte mehr Zeit mit dir verbringen.
examples.english: I'd like to spend more time with you.

words.tip: nicht mehr = no longer: Ich wohne nicht mehr hier. kein … mehr = no more: Wir haben keine Milch mehr.
Watch out: halb acht means 7:30, half way TO eight. This trips up every English speaker, so drill it with the clock.
der ganze Tag = the whole day. As an adverb it can mean 'quite' (ganz gut = pretty good) or 'completely' (ganz neu = brand new).
The comparative of gut, irregular like English: gut, besser, am besten. Es geht mir besser = I feel better.

examples.english: The two words sound the same.

words.tip: Also 'in a moment': Ich komme gleich! Bis gleich! = see you soon. das Gleiche = the same thing.

examples.english: It's different where we come from.

words.tip: Ending -s, unlike other adjectives. jemand anders = someone else. Compare things between your two countries.
The comparative of gern: gern, lieber, am liebsten. Ich mag Kaffee, aber ich trinke lieber Tee.
der Unterschied zwischen … und … = the difference between. A handy question for these sessions!

examples.english: We have to tidy up today.

words.tip: Separable: Ich räume mein Zimmer auf. Different from putzen (to clean): you can tidy without cleaning.

examples.english: Can you take the rubbish out?

words.tip: Explain Mülltrennung: separate bins for paper, plastic (gelber Sack), organic waste and the rest.
For things, but also 'exhausted': Ich bin total kaputt. Before a noun it takes endings: ein kaputtes Handy.
-ieren verbs take no ge-: ich habe es repariert. Casually also machen: Kannst du das wieder ganz machen?
The opposite is schmutzig or dreckig. Casually sauber! also means 'nice one!'.

examples.text: Was ist der Plan für heute?

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Pläne. Also a map of a city or a timetable: der Stadtplan, der Fahrplan.

examples.text: Das nächste Mal komme ich mit.

words.tip: Takes endings: nächsten Monat, nächstes Jahr. No 'the': nächste Woche. Der Nächste, bitte! = next, please.
Bis bald! = see you soon. so bald wie möglich = as soon as possible.
Bis später! = see you later. The comparative of spät, which they already know.

examples.text: Wir sprechen oft über die Zukunft.
examples.english: We often talk about the future.

words.tip: in Zukunft = from now on, in the future. A good prompt to share your plans together.
Reflexive for 'remember': sich erinnern an (Ich erinnere mich an den Tag). Without sich it's 'remind': Erinner mich bitte!

examples.text: Ich darf den Schlüssel nicht vergessen.

words.tip: Irregular: du vergisst, er vergisst. The participle is the same as the infinitive: Ich habe es vergessen.

words.gloss: in the past, used to; earlier

examples.text: Früher habe ich in Berlin gewohnt.
examples.english: I used to live in Berlin.

words.tip: German has no 'used to': früher does the job. Also simply 'earlier': Kannst du früher kommen?

examples.english: Back then we were still young.

words.tip: For one specific time in the past, while früher is more general. Tell each other a story starting with Damals…
Takes endings: letzten Monat, letztes Jahr. Like nächste, no 'the' with time words. zuletzt is the adverb.

examples.english: Can you explain that to me?

words.tip: No ge- in the past: ich habe erklärt. Takes the dative person: Ich erkläre dir das. Very useful in these sessions!

examples.text: Kannst du mir von deiner Familie erzählen?
examples.english: Can you tell me about your family?

words.tip: For stories and news; for telling someone to do something use sagen. Erzähl mal! = tell me all about it.
Two plurals: Wörter for single words, Worte for words that are said (kind words, a speech). Wörterbuch = dictionary.
Umlaut in the plural: Sätze. Also a set in tennis. Build sentences together with the words learned so far.
Fremdsprache = foreign language, Muttersprache = mother tongue. Welche Sprachen sprichst du?

examples.text: Meine Nummer fängt mit null an.

words.tip: Also in football scores: zwei zu null. Null Ahnung! = no idea at all.
No 'one' needed: hundert, or einhundert for clarity. Big numbers are one long word: hundertfünfzig.

examples.text: Die Stadt ist über tausend Jahre alt.
examples.english: The city is over a thousand years old.

words.tip: Tausend Dank! = thanks a million. Practise reading years: 1999 is neunzehnhundertneunundneunzig.
Ordinals take endings like adjectives: am ersten Mai. Dates use them: der erste Januar. Written as 1. with a dot.

examples.english: Will you give me your number?

words.tip: For phone and house numbers; a number in maths is die Zahl.
Umlaut in the plural: Flüsse. Name the big ones together: der Rhein, die Elbe, die Donau.
der See = lake, but die See = the sea! Plural Seen, said with two e sounds: 'zay-en'. der Bodensee is a famous one.

examples.text: Im Sommer fahren wir ans Meer.
examples.english: In summer we're going to the seaside.

words.tip: ans Meer fahren = go to the seaside. die Ostsee and die Nordsee are seas: that's die See, not der See.
Explain giving flowers when visiting: an odd number, and red roses only for your partner!

examples.text: Am Sonntag gehen wir im Wald spazieren.
examples.english: On Sunday we're going for a walk in the woods.

words.tip: Umlaut in the plural: Wälder. The Schwarzwald (Black Forest) and the German love of Waldspaziergänge.

examples.english: The bird sings in the morning.

words.tip: The V sounds like f. Umlaut in the plural: Vögel. Einen Vogel haben = to be a bit crazy.
Both the animal and the food. Fischbrötchen (fish roll) is a north German classic.
The pf is a tough sound: say p and f together. Ich glaub, mich tritt ein Pferd! = I don't believe it!

examples.text: Das Schwein lebt auf dem Bauernhof.
examples.english: The pig lives on the farm.

words.tip: Schwein haben = to be lucky! Also an insult. Schweinefleisch = pork.

examples.text: Die Katze spielt mit der Maus.
examples.english: The cat is playing with the mouse.

words.tip: Plural Mäuse, like mouse/mice. Also a computer mouse, and Mäuse is slang for money.
Umlaut in the plural: Bälle. Also a formal dance: der Ball. Ballspiele = ball games.
Irregular past: gewonnen. Also for prizes: im Lotto gewinnen. der Gewinner = the winner.

examples.text: Ich will nicht schon wieder verlieren!
examples.english: I don't want to lose again!

words.tip: For games and for things: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel verloren. Irregular past: verloren.

examples.text: Das Spiel fängt um acht an.

words.tip: Both a game you play and a football match. spielen = to play, and Spielzeug = toy.
In sport; at work people say das Team. Die Nationalmannschaft = the national team.
hoffen auf = to hope for. Ich hoffe es! = I hope so. hoffentlich = hopefully, very common in speech.
Umlaut in the plural: Träume. träumen = to dream, Traumhaus = dream house. Schöne Träume! = sweet dreams.

examples.english: We wish you all the best.

words.tip: Ich wünsche mir … = I wish for (e.g. for a present). der Wunsch = the wish. Was wünschst du dir?
so schnell wie möglich = as soon as possible. unmöglich = impossible. vielleicht is the everyday 'maybe'.
Both luck and happiness. Glück haben = to be lucky, zum Glück = luckily. glücklich (happy) comes from it.
Herzlich willkommen! is the warm version. For 'you're welcome' after danke, say bitte or gern geschehen.
Look each other in the eye when you clink, or it's supposed to bring bad luck. Zum Wohl! is more formal.
Only when going to bed; in the evening say guten Abend. Schlaf gut! and Träum was Schönes! often follow.
der Spaß = fun. Das macht Spaß = that's fun. The Swiss write it Spass, since they don't use ß.
Said to anyone who's ill. Besserung comes from besser: 'good getting-better'.

noun.hint: People usually take their sex: der Bruder, der Vater, die Schwester, die Mutter.

words.tip: German doesn't mark older or younger in the word itself: mein großer Bruder / mein kleiner Bruder. Geschwister = siblings.

noun.hint: People usually take their sex: die Schwester, die Mutter, der Bruder, der Vater.

words.tip: Meine große / kleine Schwester = my older / younger sister. Hast du Geschwister? = do you have brothers or sisters?
The everyday word. Großmutter is the formal one. German uses the same word for both sides of the family.

examples.text: Mein Opa ist neunzig Jahre alt.
examples.english: My grandpa is ninety years old.

words.tip: The everyday word. Großvater is the formal one. Oma und Opa together are die Großeltern.

examples.text: Ihr Sohn geht schon in die Schule.
examples.english: Her son already goes to school.

words.tip: Long o, like 'zone'. The partner word is die Tochter (daughter), plural Töchter.

noun.hint: Drinks are mostly der: der Tee, der Kaffee, der Wein. Exceptions: das Wasser, das Bier.

examples.english: I like drinking tea in the evening.

words.tip: Long e, no English 'ee' sound: it rhymes with 'say' without the glide. Grüner Tee, schwarzer Tee.

noun.hint: Drinks are mostly der, but das Bier and das Wasser are exceptions.

words.tip: When ordering, the plural usually stays unchanged: zwei Bier, bitte. Sounds just like English 'beer'.

noun.hint: Drinks are mostly der: der Wein, der Tee, der Kaffee.

examples.text: Trinkst du lieber Wein oder Bier?
examples.english: Do you prefer wine or beer?

words.tip: W sounds like English v, and ei like 'eye': 'vine'. Rotwein = red wine, Weißwein = white wine.

examples.english: We're buying a bottle of wine.

words.tip: No 'of' in German: eine Flasche Wasser, ein Glas Wein. Most bottles carry a deposit (Pfand).

examples.english: I'm very thirsty. (lit. I have great thirst)

words.tip: You have thirst in German, like Hunger: ich habe Durst. The adjective durstig exists but is less common.
You have hunger: ich habe Hunger, ich habe keinen Hunger. Hungrig (hungry) also works: ich bin hungrig.
The polite way to turn down more food. Never say ich bin voll for this: that means 'I'm drunk'.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Essen, so das Mittagessen.

words.tip: Mittag (midday) + Essen (meal). Traditionally the main hot meal of the day in Germany.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Essen, so das Abendessen.

words.tip: Abend (evening) + Essen (meal). Often a cold meal of bread and cheese, also called Abendbrot.
The food is the subject: das schmeckt mir = I like the taste. Schmeckt's? = is it good? is what hosts ask.
From wohnen. Germans count all rooms except kitchen and bathroom, so a Zweizimmerwohnung has one bedroom.

examples.text: Das Bad ist neben der Küche.
examples.english: The bathroom is next to the kitchen.

words.tip: Short for Badezimmer. The final d sounds like t: 'baht'. Ein Bad nehmen = to take a bath.

examples.text: Im Sommer essen wir im Garten.
examples.english: In summer we eat in the garden.

words.tip: Im Garten = in the garden. Kindergarten is literally a 'children's garden'.
Said 'twa-LET-te', with the French oi. Signs often say WC, pronounced 'vay-tsay'.

noun.hint: Compound nouns take the gender of their last part: das Zimmer, so das Schlafzimmer.

words.tip: schlafen + Zimmer, a 'sleep room'. The same pattern gives Wohnzimmer (living room) and Kinderzimmer.

examples.text: Kannst du bitte das Fenster öffnen?
examples.english: Can you open the window, please?

words.tip: In everyday speech people more often say aufmachen: mach das Fenster auf. Geöffnet on a shop door = open.
Everyday alternative: zumachen. Geschlossen on a door = closed. Related to der Schlüssel (key).

examples.english: We're looking for a new flat.

words.tip: No 'for' in German: ich suche meinen Schlüssel. The ch is the throaty one after u, as in Buch.

words.gloss: to find; to think (have an opinion)

examples.text: Ich kann meinen Schlüssel nicht finden.

words.tip: Also the everyday way to give an opinion: ich finde das gut = I think that's good. Wie findest du das?

examples.text: Kannst du mir das Foto zeigen?
examples.english: Can you show me the photo?

words.tip: Z sounds like ts: 'TSY-gen'. The person shown takes mir / dir: zeig mir das!

examples.text: Wir laufen jeden Morgen im Park.
examples.english: We run in the park every morning.

words.tip: In many regions it just means to go on foot. Vowel change: er läuft. Wie läuft's? = how's it going?

examples.text: Vor dem Haus stehen zwei Autos.
examples.english: There are two cars in front of the house.

words.tip: German says upright things stand: das Auto steht, die Flasche steht. Flat things lie (liegen).

examples.text: Wir sitzen gern auf dem Sofa.
examples.english: We like sitting on the sofa.

words.tip: Being seated. Sitting down is a different verb: sich setzen. Setz dich! = sit down!

examples.text: Im Sommer schwimmen wir im See.
examples.english: In summer we swim in the lake.

words.tip: Schw = 'shv'. Das Schwimmbad = swimming pool. Past tense with sein: ich bin geschwommen.

examples.text: Deine Schlüssel liegen auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: Your keys are on the table.

words.tip: For flat things and for places: Köln liegt am Rhein. Ie is a long 'ee'. Not 'to tell a lie' (that's lügen).
For length and for time. Wie lange? = how long (time). Comparative with umlaut: länger.
Short in length or time, not height: a short person is klein. Z = ts: 'koorts'.
Both meanings are common: eine schwere Frage = a hard question. Schw = 'shv'.
The opposite of schwer in both senses. Light as in bright is hell, a different word.
V sounds like f: 'foll'. For people it means drunk, so after a meal say ich bin satt. Opposite: leer.
Was ist deine Lieblingsfarbe? = what's your favourite colour? Lieblings- works in front of any noun.
Hard g, and the final b sounds like p: 'gelp'. German letterboxes and post vans are gelb.
Au as in 'cow'. Graue Haare = grey hair.
Sounds almost like English 'brown'. Braune Augen = brown eyes.

examples.text: Das Mädchen trägt ein rosa Kleid.
examples.english: The girl is wearing a pink dress.

words.tip: One of the few adjectives that never takes an ending: ein rosa Kleid, die rosa Blume. Lila (purple) is the same.
Angry at someone = wütend auf: ich bin wütend auf dich. A milder word is sauer (literally 'sour').

examples.text: Vor der Prüfung bin ich nervös.

words.tip: V here sounds like English v, and the stress is at the end: ner-VÖS. Das macht mich nervös = that makes me nervous.
Literally 'long-while-ish'. To say you are bored: mir ist langweilig. Final -ig sounds like 'ich'.
Keine Sorge! is the set phrase for 'don't worry'. Ich mache mir Sorgen = I'm worried.

examples.text: Ich bin froh, dass du da bist.

words.tip: Glad or relieved about something, whereas glücklich is deeper happiness. Frohe Weihnachten = Merry Christmas.

noun.hint: Short words from other languages ending in -o are usually das: das Büro, das Auto, das Kino.

words.tip: From French bureau; the stress is on the end: bü-RO. Im Büro = at the office.
A female colleague is die Kollegin. It adds -n in every form but the basic one: mit meinem Kollegen.
A false friend: it means boss, not cook (that's der Koch). Said 'shef'. A female boss is die Chefin.

examples.text: Ich habe morgen einen Termin beim Arzt.
examples.english: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow.

words.tip: Stress on the end: ter-MEEN. For doctors, offices and hairdressers. Meeting friends is a Treffen or Verabredung.
Two syllables: 'POW-ze'. Eine Pause machen = to take a break. Mittagspause = lunch break.
Three syllables, stress in the middle: mi-NU-te. In fünf Minuten = in five minutes.
A length of time. Clock time is Uhr: drei Stunden = three hours, drei Uhr = three o'clock. St = 'sht'.

noun.hint: Times of day are der: der Mittag, der Morgen, der Abend. The odd one out is die Nacht.

examples.text: Am Mittag ist es sehr warm.

words.tip: Mitte (middle) + Tag. Heute Mittag = at noon today. Mahlzeit! is the lunchtime greeting at work.

noun.hint: Times of day are der: der Nachmittag, der Morgen, der Abend. The odd one out is die Nacht.

examples.english: In the afternoon we go for a walk.

words.tip: nach (after) + Mittag. Am Nachmittag = in the afternoon. Heute Nachmittag = this afternoon.

noun.hint: Times of day are der: der Vormittag, der Morgen, der Abend. The odd one out is die Nacht.

examples.text: Am Vormittag arbeite ich zu Hause.
examples.english: In the morning I work from home.

words.tip: vor (before) + Mittag: roughly nine to twelve. The early morning is der Morgen.
Meiner Meinung nach… = in my opinion… Ich bin deiner Meinung = I agree with you.
W = v, and the final -ig sounds like 'ich'. Important to someone uses mir / dir: das ist mir wichtig.
Two syllables, stress at the end: i-DAY. Keine Ahnung (no idea) is the usual way to say you don't know.

words.gloss: to be right, to be correct
words.tip: Mostly heard as Das stimmt! = that's right. Stimmt so = keep the change, when you pay in a restaurant.
Usually 'funny peculiar', not 'funny ha-ha' (that's lustig). Long o: 'KOH-mish'.

noun.hint: Weather words are mostly der: der Wind, der Regen, der Schnee.

words.tip: W = v and the final d = t: 'vint'. Windig = windy: es ist windig.

noun.hint: Weather words are mostly der: der Schnee, der Regen, der Wind.

examples.text: Im Winter liegt hier viel Schnee.
examples.english: There's a lot of snow here in winter.

words.tip: Long e: 'shnay'. The verb is schneien: es schneit = it's snowing. Schneemann = snowman.

examples.english: There isn't a cloud in the sky.

words.tip: W = v: 'VOL-ke'. Bewölkt = cloudy, the word in weather forecasts.

examples.english: There are lots of stars in the sky.

words.tip: One word for sky and heaven. Am Himmel = in the sky. Um Himmels willen! = for heaven's sake!

examples.text: Heute Nacht ist der Mond voll.

words.tip: Long o, final d = t: 'mohnt'. Der Mond is masculine and die Sonne feminine, the opposite of French or Spanish. Vollmond = full moon.

examples.text: Mein Vater liest jeden Morgen die Zeitung.
examples.english: My father reads the newspaper every morning.

words.tip: Z = ts: 'TSY-toong'. Looks like Zeit (time) and is related: the news of the time.
One word for a story and for history. The ch is the soft one, as in ich. Gutenachtgeschichte = bedtime story.
Long ie, final d = t: 'leet'. Lieblingslied = favourite song. Young people also just say der Song.
fern (far) + sehen (see), a 'far-seer'. To watch TV is fernsehen: wir sehen heute Abend fern.

examples.english: The picture hangs in the living room.

words.tip: Any picture: a painting, a drawing, a photo, or the image on a screen. Final d = t: 'bilt'.
No ge- in the past because of the ver- prefix: ich habe es versucht. Trying food or clothes on is probieren.
Often with sich: ich kann mich nicht entscheiden = I can't make up my mind. Die Entscheidung = decision.

words.gloss: to choose; to vote; to dial
words.tip: Ä here is a long 'eh': 'VAY-len'. Picking something out is often aussuchen in everyday speech.
Related to anders (different). When something changes by itself, add sich: das Wetter ändert sich.
The encouragement word: Du schaffst das! = you can do it! Geschafft! = done it! (with relief).
Used for men and women alike. Zu Gast sein = to be someone's guest. Gasthaus = an inn.

examples.english: We want to invite your parents.

words.tip: Separable: ich lade dich ein. In a café, ich lade dich ein means 'it's on me'. Die Einladung = invitation.

examples.text: Darf ich dir meine Schwester vorstellen?
examples.english: May I introduce my sister to you?

words.tip: Separable: ich stelle dir Anna vor. With sich + mir it means to imagine: das kann ich mir vorstellen.
From Hof (court), like 'courteous'. Using Sie with strangers is the heart of German politeness. Opposite: unhöflich.
A female neighbour is die Nachbarin. The ch is the throaty one after a, as in Nacht.

examples.text: Ich komme, wenn ich Zeit habe.
examples.english: I'll come if I have time.

words.tip: Sends the verb to the end, like weil. Not for questions: 'when?' is wann. For one moment in the past use als.

examples.text: Ich weiß, dass du müde bist.

words.tip: Always a comma before it, and the verb goes to the end. Sounds the same as das; only the spelling differs.

examples.text: Er arbeitet, obwohl er krank ist.

words.tip: Verb to the end again. Stress on the second part: ob-VOHL.

examples.text: Es regnet, deshalb bleiben wir zu Hause.
examples.english: It's raining, so we're staying home.

words.tip: Unlike weil it doesn't send the verb to the end: the verb comes straight after it (deshalb bleiben wir).

examples.text: Ich trinke keinen Kaffee, sondern Tee.
examples.english: I don't drink coffee, but tea.

words.tip: The 'but' after a negative that corrects it: nicht A, sondern B. Otherwise 'but' is aber.
W = v, stress on the end: va-ROOM. The answer usually starts with weil. Warum nicht? = why not?
Takes the same endings as der/die/das: welcher Tag, welche Farbe, welches Buch.

examples.english: Where are we going in the summer?

words.tip: German separates where (wo, a place) from where to (wohin, a direction): Wo bist du? but Wohin gehst du?
Woher kommst du? = where are you from? With wissen it asks for the source: how do you know?
Two words. For things you can count, wie viele: wie viele Kinder? Wie viel Uhr ist es? = what time is it?
Shouted on its own it's the emergency call: Hilfe! The verb is helfen: kannst du mir helfen?

noun.hint: Nouns ending in -ei are die: die Polizei, die Bäckerei.

words.tip: Singular in German: die Polizei ist da. Stress on the end: po-li-TSY. The number is 110; fire and ambulance is 112.

examples.english: The street is dangerous at night.

words.tip: From die Gefahr (danger). The ä is a long 'eh': ge-FAIR-lich. Opposite: ungefährlich or sicher.
Vorsicht! on its own is the warning: watch out! V = f here: 'FOR-zich-tich'.
Two everyday meanings: safe, and sure. Bist du sicher? = are you sure? Sicher! = sure, of course!
Often with sich: wir streiten uns. St = 'sht'. Der Streit = the argument.
Einen Fehler machen = to make a mistake. Long e: 'FAY-ler'. Learners should make lots of them!
The person forgiven takes mir / dir. Verzeihung! is a polite 'pardon me'. Z = ts.
From die Ehre (honour). Ehrlich? as a question = really? Ehrlich gesagt… = to be honest…
Vowel change: er verspricht. Versprochen! on its own = I promise! Careful: sich versprechen = to make a slip of the tongue.
